Underside of a large leaf hanging in the canopy, with other leaves crowding the frame and the left edge close to the blade. Dappled light dulls the colour and the margin takes some study.
Trunk with trunk edges showing, vertical ridges. Grey-green lichen patches cover much of the surface, so the ridge pattern and the true colour need some study.
A forked trunk with crown and autumn forest around it; a scene, not a bark close-up. Dappled shade and sun on the trunk.
Texture-only frame with no trunk edge, branch or scale object. Ridges and plates are sharp. The orange-red cast looks like warm light, so the true colour is uncertain.
A crown of orange autumn leaves against the sky. The leaves blend into a mass and no single leaf can be traced.
Fallen autumn leaves in a pile. The central yellow leaf is mostly whole but others overlap it, so the outline and margin must be searched for.
Twig with paired green-nutlet samaras with tan wings hanging in clusters against a black background, with some leaves. The fruit is not yet ripe, so growth_stage is unripe and usual_look false.
Trunk with a branch fork, grey furrowed ridges with some moss, bare winter trees behind. The ridge pattern is a little small and mossy, so a learner has to study it (pattern search).
Mature trunk filling the frame with long, vertical, shaggy ridges and plates; brick building behind is soft and does not compete.
Camera looks up the trunk into the crown with big limbs and foliage competing; bark is foreshortened and hard to read. Angle from below makes it harder.
A single ripe tan paired samara with a short stalk on a plain purple background with a 1 cm scale bar. Sharp and complete, with no sign of how it hangs on the twig.
Trunk with irregular vertical furrows and peeling, curling plates, with leaves and a lawn behind. The pattern is readable.
Texture-only close view with no trunk edge, branch, or scale; some moss and lichen. The ridges are readable but the overall pattern repeat is harder to judge.
Mature trunk with vertical ridges and rough plates, sharp, with a brick building and foliage behind that do not compete.
Old, gnarled, forked trunk with moss, in dappled sun against tall grass and foliage. The bark detail is small in the frame and the scene competes, so the pattern is something to search for.
A single samara lying on snow with a green sprout emerging, seen from above. It is a germinating fruit lying on the ground (atypical) and a top view (angle).
Hanging cluster of paired green samaras with soft background. The nutlets are still green, so the fruit is full shape but unripe.
View from below into a crown with backlit leaves overlapping. The central lobed leaf can be traced, but it is crowded (alone false), seen from below (angle) and backlit (light).
Cluster of dark green lobed leaves seen from above, with the rounded lobes and veins readable. Neighbouring leaves fill the frame, so the subject is not alone.
One lobed leaf with several holes and small yellow-green galls. The leaf reaches the top edge of the frame so it is not fully shown. Damage changes the outline.
Branch with a cluster of samaras with green nutlets and tan wings against a black background that looks flash-lit. The flash changes the colour, and the fruit is not yet ripe.

Oak branch seen from below against the sky, with leaves overlapping and small in frame, plus a small acorn pair. The learner must search for a single outline. The view is from below (angle) and partly backlit (light).
Wet leafy branch seen from above over a mulch background. The leaves are small in the frame and crowded, so a learner finds the lobes only by looking closely.
Dry brown samaras hanging in a cluster against a soft background, lit by warm low sun that shifts the colour (light).
Close view of one pale grey-green leaf underside against a dark, shaded background. The right edge cuts off a lobe and the lower left is clipped, so it is not whole. The deep shade is a light cause.
View looking up a forked trunk into the leafy crown; the main subject is the whole tree, so the part is other. The upward angle makes it harder.
Green unripe acorns in a cluster on the twig with lobed oak leaves around them. Kind, shape, hang and cap are readable; the fruit is full size but not ripe.
Mature trunk with narrow vertical ridges and flaky scaly plates, both trunk edges in frame. Sharp and well lit.
Full trunk width with ridged, scaly plates in even light. Trunk edges show, so the frame is not too close.
Single green unripe acorn with a warty cap resting over a large leaf edge. The attachment to the twig is not shown, so hang is no.
A drooping branch with many deeply lobed leaves overlapping in a crowd. A learner can find single outlines only with study, so shape and margin are search and alone is false.
Trunk with small blocky plates in a forest, with understory and other trunks behind it. The bark is readable; the busy background lowers alone.
Trunk with patchy sun and shadow across it that hides the ridge pattern and changes the colour, so pattern and colour are search. Light is the cause.
Grey trunk with fine shallow scaly ridges in soft light. The fine pattern needs close study to trace, so pattern is search.
Two ripe acorns on a plain blue studio background, one with its warty cap and one bare, with a 1 cm scale bar. Both nuts are whole and sharp.
Brown dead leaf litter on the ground with hard shadows; leaves overlap and the subject is a dead leaf. Outline is only traceable with close study.
Three full-size green acorns with warty caps sit on a twig among lobed leaves. The acorns are not ripe, so the usual look is false.
Cluster of green, full-shape acorns with scaly caps on the twig, with leaves around. Unripe, so not the usual look.
A whole tree crown in red autumn colour among conifers. The main subject is a whole tree, so the part is other.
A branch with red autumn leaves against a soft dark background. The leaves overlap and are small and soft, so lobes and margin need close study. Autumn colour, so not the usual look.
Green lobed leaves with bristle-tipped lobes seen from above on a small plant, with more leaves and litter behind. The top view is slightly unusual.
Close view of ripe acorns with warty caps on a twig. The pink-purple colour cast and dark background shift the colour, so light.
Underside of one green leaf with pointed, bristle-tipped lobes and clear veins, seen against the sky and trees. The underside view is less usual, so angle.
A single green acorn with a scaly cap on a twig, with leaves behind. Full shape but not ripe.
Yellow-orange new leaves at a shoot tip, sunlit and overlapping, with busy foliage behind. Young leaves and strong sun change the colour.

Trunk shot from the base looking straight up into the crown. The camera looks up into the crown, so it is a bark_up_or_dark reject; the ridges foreshorten toward the top, so the pattern is only found with study (angle).

Several overlapping lobed leaves over a busy leaf-litter background. The centre leaf outline can be read, but the bristle tips are small and the leaves crowd each other, so alone is false and margin is search.

Mature green leaves on a branch against a soft, blurred background. Pointed lobes and bristle tips are readable. The leaves overlap a little, but the soft background keeps the subject alone. The twig shows only part of the stalk joins, so arrangement is search.

Newly expanded pale-green leaves on a twig with small catkins, with a soft background. The leaves are young and not fully shaped, and the bright translucent light shifts the colour (young, light). The catkins are small and do not replace the leaf as the subject.

Three or four broad, shallowly lobed leaves joined at a point and held against a mossy trunk. The outline and margin read clearly. The twig is mostly hidden, so arrangement is search. The leaf form is somewhat broad and might be a shoot form, but the source does not say so and I did not reject it.

Mature lobed leaves on a branch, with several leaves overlapping and crowded in the frame. The large left-centre leaf outline can be traced, but the bristle tips need close study, so margin is search and alone is false.

Trunk shot looking up into a large crown, with the bark dark against a bright sky. The camera looks up and the bark is dark and foreshortened, so it is a bark_up_or_dark reject (angle, light). The crown competes with the trunk.

Small, newly emerging yellow-green leaves overlapping, with long hanging catkins in strong backlight. The leaves are young and not fully shaped, and the backlight washes their colour (young, light). Leaves and catkins crowd each other, so no single leaf shows in full. The leaves still show, so I did not call it a buds_or_flowers reject.
A dense mass of red autumn foliage and branches. No single leaf outline can be read, so the leaves blend into a mass. Autumn colour is the growth stage, not a cause.
Full base of a large old trunk, with long vertical ridges and furrows clear and sharp. Trunk edges and the ground are in frame. A small tag at the upper left is not a readable name label.

Close-up of ridged, scaly bark with lichen and warm low sun; no trunk edge, branch or scale, so too close. The ridge pattern repeat is readable only on study, so pattern is search, and the warm light shifts the colour.
Newly unfolding tulip tree leaves on a twig against soft blue sky. The leaves have not reached full shape and one is folded, so the lobes need close study, but the leaf stalks join the twig.
Single brown acorn hanging from its twig with a scaly cap, against a soft green background. Sharp and complete.
Five ripe acorns with caps lying on a plain light surface, sharp and complete. They do not hang on a twig, so hang is no.
Seed-collection style photo of an acorn with its cap plus a cut and an end-on view of the nut, on a plain blue background with a 1 cm scale bar. No twig, so hang is no.
Tulip tree foliage with several open flowers; the main subject is the flowers within a crowd of leaves, so the part is other.
Overlapping tulip tree leaves in a dense cluster with a bud; the leaves crowd the frame, no single outline is fully shown, and the lead leaf is tilted, so shape and margin are search.
Acorn with cap shown from several sides on a black background; sharp, complete and uncluttered. No twig, so hang is no.
Green unripe acorns on a twig, with the twig, buds and leaves around them competing, so alone is false. Full shape but not ripe.
Whole trunk face with vertical ridges and the trunk edges visible, even light and sharp.
Crown seen from below with many yellow and green leaves blending into a mass against the sky. No single leaf outline can be traced; viewed from below, hence angle.
Branches and crown with green leaves and a few orange tulip-shaped flowers; the main subject is the crown, so the part is other.
Whole trunk width with fine interlacing ridges and furrows, with some lichen patches. A street and a building are behind it, but the trunk dominates the frame.
One whole green tulip-shaped leaf on a dark background with pale prominent veins, probably the underside. A few small spots do not change the outline.
One whole green leaf held against a dark background of fallen yellow leaves, which signal autumn. The outline and the notched top are clear; the leaf itself is still green and mature.
Many overlapping leaves on a branch with a small bud. Single outlines can be found only with study, so the key features are search and the subject is crowded.
Two open yellow-orange flowers and a bud on a twig among leaves. The flowers are the main subject, so the part is other.
Top of a crown seen from below against a blue sky, in warm low sun. The subject is a crown, so the part is other.
Frame filled with vertical ridges and furrows, with no trunk edge, branch or scale object, so it is too close. The ridge pattern is readable.
Seedling-type leaves with irregular wavy lobes among other low plants on the ground. The form is young and not the typical mature leaf, and the leaves compete with the background.
A full trunk with deep, narrow, interlacing ridges against dark foliage and sky. Trunk edges show and the pattern reads well.
Close crop of long vertical ridges and furrows with no trunk edge, branch or scale. Yellow lichen covers much of the surface, so the true bark colour takes study.
The camera looks up the trunk into the crown, so foliage and branches compete and the bark is foreshortened. The view from below is the reject case.
A whole trunk width with ridges and pale patches, sharp, with both trunk edges visible. The background is soft.
Two children stand in front of a very large trunk. The bark is small in the frame and softly lit, so the ridges are found only with study, and the children compete for attention.
A trunk with clear furrows and pale ridges against sky, edges visible, sharp and well lit.
Texture-only close view of diagonal interlacing ridges with some lichen. No trunk edge, branch or scale shows, so it is too close.
A dark, shaded trunk base in a forest with fallen autumn leaves and many competing saplings. The ridges can be traced only with close study because of the deep shade and distance.
Several bare winter trunks, one dark and one with vines, among bare twigs. The fine ridges on the pale trunks are small in the frame, so they need study.
Dry brown cone of samaras on a twig against a soft green background; shape and kind read easily and it sits on the twig. The wings are visible only with close study.
Top view of a spread-open fruit cone on snow, so the samaras fan out like a flower. This is an unusual angle and not the typical closed form; the wings are clear but how it hangs is not shown.
Green unripe fruit of full shape, upright on the twig among leaves. The outline is clear, but the kind of fruit is hard to read when green and closed, and the wings are not visible.
Dry fruit cone against a black background, apparently lit by flash, which changes the colour. Shape and kind are clear, but the twig is cut off so the hang is not shown.
Two small fruit cones on a twig, set against autumn foliage. The fruits are small in the frame, so kind and shape need close study.
Frosted fruit cones on bare twigs against a soft blue background. The main cone is clear and shows how it sits on the twig; the frost hides the wings somewhat.
Weathered pale fruit cone lying on the ground among dry stems and debris, seen from above. The clutter competes with the subject and the form is faded.
Brown ripe fruit cone at the end of a twig against a soft autumn background with yellow leaves. Kind and shape are clear, and the individual wings need close study.
Pale fruit cone on a bare twig against a blue sky. The outline is clear, but it is small and the individual wings are hard to make out.
Crown of a tree in autumn with a mass of twigs and small leaves and fruit against the sky. No single leaf, fruit, or bark is the main subject.

A dry tulip-tree fruit cone in snow, mostly opened after seed fall, with the upright wings spread like petals and a curved stalk below. The open, spent cone is not the typical ripe form, so it is atypical and not the usual look.
Bare branches against a blue sky seen from below. The main subject is the crown, and the few small dry fruit cones are tiny in the frame, so the part is other.

A leafy shoot tip with overlapping leaves, several red-brown and still soft, which looks like young growth. The upper left leaf shows its lobes, but the margin is small in the frame and the leaves crowd each other.
A large green sycamore leaf on a dark background with the toothed edge, lobes and veins easy to read. A second leaf and the twig show the stalk joins at the top.
A leafy sapling or crown whose leaves blend into a mass. No single leaf outline or margin can be read.

A dull green leaf, seen from the underside, with small dark spots and other leaves overlapping its edges and the frame edge. The lobes and teeth can be read, but the leaf is not shown in full and it competes with its neighbours.

Two pale green leaves held by a person in front of patchy sycamore bark, with leaf litter on the ground. The hand covers part of the right leaf, the edge has low contrast, and the bark behind competes with the leaves.
A sunlit leafy shoot on a dark autumn-coloured background. The upper leaves show lobes and the alternate stalks on the twig, but the leaves overlap and the teeth are small in the frame.

A leaf seen from below, lit from behind so it glows yellow-green, with other shaded leaves above and a street behind. The view from below and the backlight make it harder, and the other leaves compete with it.

One whole green maplelike leaf with toothed lobes against a black background, flash lit. The twig and stalk are at the top but the join is small, so arrangement is search; flash on a dark background gives light.
Forked trunks of an old tree with mottled peeling bark, seen from a distance in a leafy scene. Foliage competes, and the pattern is small in the frame, so texture and pattern are search.
One whole pale green leaf with pointed lobes and a toothed edge against plain sand, with a few other leaves at the top edge. The stalk does not show where it joins the twig, so arrangement is no.
A bare winter crown with forked limbs against blue sky. The main subject is the whole tree, so the part is other.

A leafy shoot laid on a pale wooden deck, showing several lobed toothed leaves with stalks joining the stem. The leaves overlap and the deck boards add a little clutter, so alone is false; no scale object.
The base of a street trunk with dark shaded bark and pale peeling patches near the roots. A car, curb and road compete, and the pattern is small and in shade, so features are search.
A trunk with pale and olive peeling plates, clearly readable, with a branch crossing the upper part of the frame. The branch competes with the trunk, so alone is false.
The camera looks up at a pale mottled trunk and branches against the sky and bare twigs. The view from below is the unusual angle, and twigs cross the trunk, so alone is false.
A tight view of mottled olive, cream and brown bark with the camouflage pattern fully readable. The frame shows texture only, with no trunk edge, branch or scale, so too_close is true.

Several overlapping bright green lobed leaves, with one large leaf whole and sharp, and a stalk and small fruit head near the top. The leaves are crowded so alone is false, and the stalk joins are small so arrangement is search.
A green, full-shape spiky seed ball on a stalk against a leaf. It is not ripe, so growth_stage is unripe and usual_look false; the stalk is cut off from any twig, so hang is no.

Trunk base beside a curb with a parked car and grass in frame. The dark lower bark with pale patches is seen from a distance, so texture and pattern need a search, and the curb and car compete for attention.
A bare crown with pale upper limbs seen from below against blue sky. The main subject is the whole tree, so the part is other; the view from below is an unusual angle.

A weathered, decaying seed ball lying on a log with a second broken ball and leaf litter beside it. The fruit has lost its seeds and its fuzz, so it is not the typical form, and the log and litter compete with it.
A trunk with flaking plates that expose pale inner bark, filling the frame with trunk edges in view. The peeling pattern reads clearly; the woodland behind it is busy but soft.
Many small seed balls hang on bare twigs against a plain sky. They are small in the frame, so the kind and shape need a search, but how they hang is clear.
A whole trunk and crown seen from below, with pale limbs and a leafy canopy. The main subject is the tree as a whole, so the part is other; the view looks up at it.
A ripe seed ball hangs from its stalk against a soft background. Strong low sun warms the colour of the ball.
A close view of mottled, flaking bark with a burl, with no trunk edge, branch, or scale object in the frame. The plates and patches read clearly across a wide area.
A smooth, mottled trunk with trunk edges in view, partly covered by leaves and a small yellow-flowered twig in front. The leaves crowd the trunk, so the pattern takes a search.
A seed ball that has broken apart and shows fluffy fibres, hanging from a short stalk against a soft sky. The broken form is atypical, so kind and shape take study.
Many small seed balls hang on long stalks from bare twigs against plain blue sky. The balls are small in the frame, so kind and shape are at search; hang is clear.
A green mature leaf held in a hand, showing the underside with clear veins. The right edge is cut off by the frame, other leaves crowd behind, and a gall and a brown patch damage the blade.
A single seed ball hangs on a long stalk from a twig against a soft green background. New leaves and a stipule show a spring season; the ball is dry and brown.

A yellow-green full-shaped seed ball on a stalk among bare twigs. It is not yet ripe, so unripe and usual_look false.
One seed ball hangs on a long thin stalk from bare twigs against a soft grey background. All features read clearly.

Sharp green maple-like leaves in front of soft patchy bark; the leaves overlap each other and the warm film tint shifts the colour, so margin and venation take study. Bark behind is out of focus, so the leaf is the subject.
One big dark green leaf upper side against a trunk, with a hand at the top. The side lobes touch the frame edges, so the outline is not whole.
A crown full of overlapping leaves and twigs, with no single leaf outline to read. Dappled light adds to the clutter.
Whole trunk width with grey-green, cream and brown flaking patches; both trunk edges show.
Sharp trunk in bright light showing the mottled flaking plates; soft background of sky and water.
Large lobed leaf held in a hand with other leaves behind and one overlapping at the top; small spots do not change the outline.
Brown dead leaf lying on grass among other fallen leaves; autumn state and dead subject.
Branch of leaves in a crown with one small green seed ball at the lower right and a car and street behind; no single part is the subject.
Street scene with a row of trees and cyclists; the trees are the scene, not a leaf, bark or fruit subject.
One sharp green lobed leaf upper side on a dark soft background; outline and toothed edge are easy to read.

Bare, forked old trunk shot looking up toward the crown. The camera looks up and the bark is dark and knobby, so the plate pattern is hard to read.
Whole trunk width with fine pale and grey mottled plates, both edges visible, plain background of palms. Pattern and colour read well.

Large lobed green leaves in sunlight against sky with a peeling trunk at right. Leaves crowd each other and the wires and trunk compete, so margin and venation need a search. Bright backlight washes some leaves.
Rough, scaly old bark filling the frame with no trunk edge. Deep shadow on the right hides detail and shifts the colour, so pattern and colour need a search.
Close view of camouflage-like patches in green, yellow, cream and brown. Texture only with no trunk edge or scale; the pattern and colour are clear.
Narrow trunk with both edges in frame, showing flaking brown and cream plates. A small file but sharp, with a building behind that does not compete.

Crown view where many overlapping green leaves blend into a mass; no single leaf outline stands out. Two small seed balls are tiny in the frame.
A green, spiky seed ball held on its stalk in a hand with a big leaf behind. The hand and leaf compete with the ball, and the hold hides how it hangs. Only one ball shows.
A fallen, breaking-up seed ball on paving, seen from above, with released fluffy seeds beside it. Atypical form and top view make it harder; the outline is ragged.
A scene of a trunk, brown leaves and warm low sun, with one small green seed ball in the middle. The main subject is the scene, so the part is other.
One whole green spiky seed ball hanging on a long stalk, with leaves behind it. Kind, shape and hang read well. Only one ball, so no two heads.
A green seed ball hanging from a thin stalk against a soft green background. The ball is the only subject. One ball only.
Two brown seed balls against a soft blue-sky background on bare twigs. It is hard to tell whether both sit on one stalk, so two_heads needs a close look.
Several dark seed balls seen from below against blue sky, with branches crossing the frame. The balls are dark and backlit, and each hangs on its own stalk, so no two heads.
A small dark seed ball in the middle of a frame full of leaves, seen from below and backlit. The ball is small and dark, so its kind and shape need a search.
Two green seed balls hang one below the other on a single stalk, with leaves behind in soft focus. A second ball sits at the stalk end, so two_heads is clear.

A single brown, bristly seed ball held in a hand, fully in frame against a soft leaf-litter background. Kind and shape read clearly; only a short stalk stub shows, so hang is no, and there is only one ball, so two_heads is no.

One whole three-lobed leaf in red, orange and green autumn colour, with its outline and toothed edge readable against conifer needles. Autumn colour is not a cause; it sets growth_stage autumn and usual_look false. No stalk-to-twig join and no scale in frame.

Backlit cluster of overlapping autumn leaves on a twig, soft and translucent, with the top leaf cut by the frame edge. Lobes and teeth can be traced only with study, so shape and margin are search; the backlight is the cause `light`.

A carpet of fallen leaves seen from above, red maple leaves mixed with grey and brown ones, all overlapping into a mass. No single leaf shows its margin, and only one or two outlines can be found with a search.

Many large leaves on a small stem in front of a pale trunk, turning from green to red. Several whole three-lobed leaves with toothed edges are readable, but the leaves crowd each other so alone is false. Autumn colour sets growth_stage autumn and usual_look false.

One red fallen leaf, whole and sharp, lying on brown leaf litter with a mushroom above it. Lobes, tips and teeth are readable; a few small dark spots do not change the outline. Autumn colour sets growth_stage autumn and usual_look false.

Green mature leaves on a branch with red leaf stalks, sharply lit against a dark background. Whole lobed leaves with toothed edges are readable, but the leaves overlap so alone is false. Stalks meet the twig only small, so arrangement is search.
A whole small tree in red, orange and yellow autumn colour beside a lake, with its top cut by the frame. The main subject is the tree and not one leaf, so the part is other.

A cluster of autumn leaves in yellow, orange, red and green on a stem, with red leaf stalks joining the stem in pairs. Whole three-lobed leaves with toothed edges are readable, but the leaves crowd each other so alone is false. Autumn colour sets growth_stage autumn and usual_look false.

One whole green mature leaf with a red stalk against a soft dark background. Lobes, tips and coarse teeth are sharp and readable. The stalk leaves the frame without showing a twig join, and no scale is in frame.

One large leaf filling the frame, red in the middle and green at the edges, with its left lobe cut by the frame edge so whole is false. Veins, lobes and teeth are sharp. Autumn colour sets growth_stage autumn and usual_look false.

A branch packed with overlapping yellow autumn leaves, with a red tree and a building behind. The leaves overlap and blend into a mass, no single leaf shows its lobes, and no margin can be read at this size, so margin is no. Autumn colour is growth_stage autumn and not a cause.
A whole mature trunk seen from a distance in a park, with moss on the lower part and vertical furrows. The ridges are small in the frame, so texture and pattern are search.
A trunk that splits into three stems, seen from a few metres. The grey vertical furrows show on the right stem but are soft and small in the frame, so texture and pattern are search.

A close-up of grey bark with scaly ridges, flat plates and some lichen. It shows texture only, with no trunk edge, branch or scale object, so too_close is true. The ridges and plates are sharp and readable.
A full-width mature trunk in even light, with long narrow vertical ridges and strips, and both trunk edges in frame. The pattern is sharp and the background is soft green.

A trunk at medium distance with brown furrows and pale patches, and both trunk edges in frame. A thin twig lies across the left side and competes slightly, but the pattern is readable. The growth stage is mature, though the pale patches could be read as a younger bark.

The camera looks steeply up the trunk toward the crown, with a strong sun flare at the upper right. A birdhouse on the trunk competes with the bark, and its 'Love' text is not a plant name label. The view from below is angle, the flare and backlight are light, and the ridges are foreshortened.

Red-pink samara pairs hang on red stalks from a dark twig against blue sky and a soft reddish background. The lower cluster is sharp and shows the paired wings and the way they hang.

Pale pink-tan samara clusters hang among young leaves and branches in a crown, with sky and a building behind. The fruit is small and crowded by leaves, so kind, shape and wing need close study (search), but the hang from the branch is visible.
A frame-filling view of grey-tan bark with vertical ridges and flaking scales in even light. It has no trunk edge, branch or scale object, so it is too close, but the ridge pattern repeats clearly.
Sharp red-pink samara pairs hang on red stalks from a twig, with a young leaf at upper left and a soft green background. The cluster is whole and the wings and the hang are easy to read.

Very young red-green samaras with small wings sit on upright stems among spent flower parts, against a soft dark background. The fruit has not reached its full shape, so kind, shape and wing need close study; the twig attachment is only partly shown.

One whole five-lobed leaf hangs on its long stalk against a near-black background; outline, lobe tips and edge are easy to read. Flash against the dark scene turns the blade grey-green, so I set light; the pale blade and raised veins suggest the underside.

Sharp clusters of red paired samaras hang from a bare twig against a soft, blurred background. Wings are full size but the seed bodies are still green-yellow and the wings bright red, so I judged them unripe, not young.

Green lobed leaves on a branch crossed by a twig, with other leaves overlapping; the main left leaf is cut off by the frame edge and tilted, so whole is false, alone is false and angle is set. The lobes can still be traced with effort and the brown spots do not change the outline.

Long garlands of orange-red paired samaras hang from leafless twigs against a black background, shot with flash. The flash gives an orange cast and a pale branch crosses the frame, but kind, shape, wings and hang are all readable; I took the orange-brown tone as ripe.

A single whole green five-lobed leaf with its stalk, flat on a plain black background (a scan or flat lay). Outline, lobe tips, edge and veins are all sharp, with nothing to show leaf arrangement or size.
A twig with hanging clusters of small red flowers on long thin stalks, against a soft overcast sky. Flowers only, with no leaf or fruit showing, so part is other and buds_or_flowers applies.

A fallen yellow-red autumn leaf lies on a pile of overlapping leaves; its right side runs off the frame edge and its left is overlapped, so whole and alone are false. Bright red paired samaras hang in clusters from a twig against a clean blue sky, sharp and easy to read. The seed bodies are still yellow-green and the wings fresh red, so I judged them unripe with full shape.

One whole green five-lobed leaf with its stalk lies flat on wood-chip mulch; the leaf fills most of the frame and its outline and edge stand out from the brown chips. The dull grey-green blade with raised pale veins suggests the underside.
A close view of a crown full of orange autumn foliage with branches and sky between; no single leaf stands out and the leaves blend into a mass. Part is other (crown) and leaf_mass applies.
Mature trunk with vertical ridges and flaking plates, both trunk edges in frame, brick building soft behind. Nothing makes it harder.
One whole green leaf, upper side, on a white backdrop with soft shadows; outline, edge and veins read easily. No twig or scale shows, so arrangement and size are no.
A small sapling standing in a garden bed with hostas in front and an evergreen hedge behind. The main subject is the whole young plant, so the part is other.
One large leaf seen from the pale underside, hanging among other leaves with a second leaf overlapping at lower right, so alone is false. The outline and edge still read against the dark foliage.
Mature trunk with long vertical ridges and grey-green lichen patches, both trunk edges in frame. A thin vine crosses the trunk but does not hide the ridges.

Wide shot of a large old forked trunk with deep furrows, shot from low and tilted up toward the autumn crown, so angle; the ridge pattern is seen from a distance (search) against a busy forest background. Strong sun and shade stripes and warm foliage light change the trunk colour.
Tight crop of deeply fissured bark with flaking plates and no trunk edge, branch or scale, so too_close. The orange-red tint looks like warm light, so light.
A small sapling in a garden bed with hostas below and a spruce trunk, fence and house behind. The main subject is the whole young plant, so the part is other.
Crown of red and orange autumn foliage filling the frame with branches and sky showing through; the leaves blend into a mass, so the part is other.

Pile of fallen yellow and orange leaves with a few brown ones, overlapping so no outline is complete; outline and edge need close study, so crowded (alone false) and key features at search. Autumn colour, so growth stage autumn and not the usual look.

A leafy twig on a black background with a hanging cluster of maple samaras; I set part to fruit because the samara cluster is the focal point, though the leaves take equal space. The seed bodies are green and the wings pale, so the fruit is full shape but unripe (unripe, usual_look false); the samaras overlap and are small, so shape is search.

A wide old trunk with a branch fork, grey furrowed bark with moss and lichen patches, bare trees and blue sky behind. The ridges are soft and mottled by lichen, so a learner has to look closely to read the ridge pattern (pattern search).

A mature trunk fills the frame, with long vertical ridges and curling plates and reddish wound patches; trunk edges and a brick building are visible. Sharp and well lit, so texture and pattern are readable.

The camera looks straight up an old trunk into the crown with large limbs and a burl, so this is a view from below (angle). The trunk bark is foreshortened and the crown and branches compete in the frame, so the ridge pattern is search and alone is false.
One dry, tan, ripe double samara lying flat on a plain lilac background with a 1 cm scale bar; the outline and both wings are sharp. It is not on a twig, so hang is no.

A sunlit mature trunk with deep vertical furrows and shaggy, flaking plates; both trunk edges are in frame and the background (trees, road, building) is soft. The ridge and plate pattern reads clearly.

A close-up of rough grey bark with moss and lichen filling the frame: no trunk edge, branch, or scale object, so too_close is true. The texture is sharp, but without the trunk shape the overall ridge pattern needs close study (pattern search).

A tight crop of grey bark with long vertical ridges and curling plates, orange-brown showing in the furrows; no trunk edge, branch, or scale object, so too_close is true. Sharp and evenly lit, so texture and pattern are readable.

An old, gnarled trunk with low limbs in a grassy field, pale peeling bark patched with moss. The bark is seen from a distance, so texture and pattern are search; the grass and surrounding trees compete, so alone is false.

A single fallen samara lies on snow, seen from above, with a green radicle growing out of the seed end. Atypical because it is germinating, angle because it is a top view of a fruit lying flat, and it shows no hang.
A sharp cluster of paired samaras hangs on long stalks from a twig. The wings are full size but the seed bodies are still green, so it is unripe and not the usual look.

Lobed leaves on a branch seen from below against sky and trunk, with the underside showing. The central leaf is whole and readable, but overlapping leaves crowd it (alone false) and the view from below is an angle cause.

A tight cluster of large lobed leaves at a twig tip, overlapping and crowded, with several whole outlines readable. The shaded, cool grey-green cast changes the leaf colour (light), and the stalks that join the twig are mostly hidden.

One sharp lobed leaf against a soft background, with several round holes and a cluster of small yellow galls at the lower right edge (damaged). The leaf base runs off the top of the frame, so whole is false.
A twig with many paired samaras against a plain black background, with green seed bodies and tan wings, so unripe. The flash-style lighting on black changes the colours (light).

A leafy branch with deeply lobed leaves, taking the leaves as the main subject because they fill most of the frame. Two small acorns sit at the centre, too small to be the subject. Foliage is crowded so alone is false, and venation and arrangement take a search.

Many small wet lobed leaves on a low branch over red mulch. They are crowded and small in the frame, so every key feature needs a search. Single leaf outlines can still be traced, so it does not read as a mass.
Dry brown paired samaras hang in a cluster from thin stalks against a soft blurred background. Warm low backlit sun tints the wings (light).

One large lobed leaf fills the frame against a dark soft background, tilted toward the camera with the grey-green underside showing (angle). The shaded, cool cast changes the colour (light), and the base and right lobe tips touch the frame edge, so whole is false.

A whole tree seen from the ground: the trunk forks into two big limbs under a leafy crown against the sky, so the main subject is the tree, not a bark area. The view from below is an unusual angle; if this were read as bark, it would be a bark_up_or_dark case.
Green acorns with warty caps sit in a cluster on a twig, with lobed leaves behind them. The nuts are full shape but still green, so unripe and not the usual look; the twig shows how they sit.
A wide trunk area of grey-brown, scaly, ridged plates in even shade, with the trunk edges and another tree and a building in the background. The ridge and plate pattern reads at a glance.
A sharp, evenly lit trunk of grey bark with narrow vertical ridges and blocky plates. The trunk edges show at both sides, so it is not texture only.

A yellow-green acorn with a warty cap on a soft background; a large lobed leaf in the foreground hides its base, so the whole fruit does not show. The twig is not visible, so hang is no, and the acorn is not ripe.

A branch of deeply lobed green leaves in strong sun, many overlapping and hanging at a tilt, over a lawn. A few centre leaves can be traced, but the crowd means a learner must search for one outline, so alone is false and shape and margin are search.
A big trunk of dark, rough ridged bark with a brick building behind it. A strong sun streak and deep shade patches change the colour across the trunk, so colour is search; the ridges still read.
A grey trunk with shallow, scaly plates and fine cracks, in clear daylight with the trunk edges, mulch and a brick building in view. The ridges are low but readable.

Two ripe, tan-orange acorns on a plain blue studio background, one nut bare and one with its warty cap, with a 1 cm scale bar. The blue is a studio backdrop and the acorn colour looks natural, so this is not a filter; there is no twig, so hang is no.

A pile of dry brown fallen oak leaves overlaps in hard low sun with deep cast shadows, so the central leaf outline is partly covered and the lobes are hard to trace. The subject is dead brown leaves (dead_leaf), the pile is crowded (alone false), and the light is harsh (light).

Three green acorns with warty caps sit at the end of a twig against soft green leaves and background, sharp and fully in view. They are full-size but still green, so growth stage is unripe and not the usual look.

A cluster of green acorns with warty caps hangs on a twig, sharp, with leaves around and a blurred hand holding the branch at the upper left. The acorns are full-size but green, so unripe and not the usual look.

A whole red autumn tree crown seen from a distance among conifers, so the main subject is the tree and no leaf, bark or fruit feature can be read. The crown is cut off at the left and bottom edges and the leaves blend into a mass.

A twig with red autumn leaves against a soft dark conifer background. The leaves overlap, are small in the frame and a little soft, so the pointed lobes and edge are found only with study; the autumn colour sets growth stage and is not a cause.

A top view of a small shoot with several green lobed leaves against blurred forest-floor litter. The pointed lobes of the lower leaves read clearly, but the leaves are small in the frame so the edge needs a closer look, and the stalks join at a single point.

A cluster of brown-pink acorns with warty caps against a dark background, lit by flash with a cool cast, and the way they sit on the twig is seen only in part. The colour looks like ripening acorns and not a heavy filter, so I did not escalate.

One large green leaf seen from below, showing its underside with the pale midrib and veins, deep sinuses and pointed bristle-tipped lobes, sharp against a leafy background. The stalk leaves the frame at the left so the twig join is not shown; a few small spots do not change the outline.
A single green acorn with a warty cap hangs from a twig, sharp against soft leaves. It is full-size but not ripe, so unripe and not the usual look.

A shoot tip of orange and yellow leaves in bright, warm sun against dark green leaves; the lobes read for the larger leaves but the edge is small and the leaves overlap. The orange colour is autumn colour, and the strong warm light also shifts the colour (light).

Several green lobed leaves overlap on a low branch above a busy leaf-litter floor, so the subject competes with its surroundings (alone false). The central leaf outline and lobes read well, but the bristle tips and veins are small in the frame and need close study.

Sharp green leaves with pointed, bristle-tipped lobes on a branch, against a soft background. The leaves overlap and the frame edge cuts off the right and lower leaves, so whole is false; where the stalks join the twig takes a search.

Newly opened pale yellow-green leaves with hanging catkins (the spring sign) in strong sun against a soft green background. The leaves are young and the sunlit, glowing colour is shifted by the light; the lobes and edge are still readable, and the catkins do not replace the leaf.

A spray of overlapping green lobed leaves on a thin twig, with a small trunk behind. The left-centre leaf is sharp and its lobes read, but the leaves are crowded (alone false) and the bristle tips are small, so margin needs a search.
A whole-tree view looking up a dark trunk into a full green crown. The crown and tree are the subject, not a bark, leaf or fruit close-up, so the part is other; the view from below is the angle.

A wide area of mature grey trunk bark with long vertical ridges and furrows, sharp, with both trunk edges and the forest background in frame. Pattern repeat, texture and colour are all easy to read.

A crown and branch scene with trunk, many leaves and a few orange-yellow tulip flowers; no single leaf, bark area or fruit is the main subject.
A whole trunk with both edges visible against a soft street background. Large grey lichen patches and fine shallow ridges make the ridge pattern readable only with some study.
One whole green leaf, pale side with prominent veins, against a dark bark background; the notched apex, lobes and smooth edge are clear. A few tiny spots do not change the outline.
One whole green leaf with notched apex and clear veins on a dark, soft background of fallen yellow leaves. The leaf is green and mature, but the leaf litter shows the season is autumn.

Many green leaves overlap on a branch, some cut by the frame, with a small bud and leaf stalks joining the twig near the centre. A learner can trace one outline only with study because the leaves crowd each other.
Two open yellow-green and orange tulip flowers and a bud on a twig, with leaves cut off by the frame, against a dark soft background. The main subject is flowers, so the part is other.
A crown tip with a branch seen from below against a plain blue sky, leaves small and warm-lit by low sun. No single leaf, bark area or fruit is the subject.

A straight mature trunk with vertical ridges and furrows that interlace, sharp, both trunk edges in frame against a dark soft background. Grey-brown colour reads true; nothing makes it harder.

Texture-only close-up of deep vertical ridges and furrows with no trunk edge, branch, or scale in frame, so too_close. Yellow-green lichen covers much of the surface, so the true bark colour takes a search.

A mature trunk with deep vertical furrows and pale ridge faces, both trunk edges in frame against plain blue sky. Sharp and bright; nothing makes it harder.

Texture-only close-up of old bark with diagonal interlacing ridges forming a lattice, with grey and yellow lichen patches; no trunk edge, branch, or scale in frame, so too_close. The ridge pattern is sharp and readable.

A green, full-shaped but unripe aggregate fruit stands upright on its twig among leaves, sharp against a soft background. The samaras are still closed into a smooth green spindle, so kind needs study and the wings are not visible.

Two small dry cones sit upright at twig tips against soft autumn foliage. The fruit is small in the frame, so kind, shape and wings need close study, though how they sit on the twig is clear.

Frosted dry cones sit upright on twigs, with the central one sharp against a deep blue, cold-toned blur. Frost covers the samara surfaces, so kind and wings need study, and the cold blue light shifts the colours (light).

A weathered, bleached cone lies on the ground in dry grass, leaf litter and clover that blend with its pale samaras and compete with it. It is not on a twig, so hang is no, and the outline takes study to trace.
A ripe brown cone of samaras with its wings spreading, sharp against a soft lawn and yellowing leaves. Its base is short and the twig is only partly visible, so hang needs study.
A pale, dry, intact cone sits upright on a bare twig against soft blue sky and branches. The samaras are packed tight with only their tips showing, so the wings need study.

A view up into a thin autumn crown against cloudy sky: bare twigs, scattered yellow leaves and tiny fruit specks. No single leaf, fruit or bark can be read, so the part is other, and the angle is from below.

A spent, upright tulip-tree fruit cluster on a twig against plain snow, with most samaras shed so the remaining winged scales fan out like a dry flower. Bare branches of a crown seen from below against blue sky, with a few tiny dried fruit remnants far too small to read as the subject. The main subject is a crown, so the part is other, and the view is upward.

An upright shoot with overlapping leaves in yellow-green, red-brown and orange, seen from below and partly backlit by the sky. The top-left leaf shows its lobed outline in full, but the leaves crowd each other, the edge teeth are small, and the angle and backlight make it harder; the colour mix reads as autumn (it could be new red growth).

One large green leaf in the foreground against soft lawn, with its palmate outline, pointed lobes, toothed edge and pale veins all readable. The twig and stalk joins sit behind other leaves at the top, so the arrangement needs a search.

A dense sapling or shoot thicket in front of a larger tree, where the leaves overlap and blend into one green mass. Only one or two lobed outlines can be found with effort and no leaf edge can be read.

A dull green leaf with dark speckles and a few blotches, lying over other leaves on leaf litter. Its toothed edge and pale veins show, but the left lobe is tucked under a neighbouring leaf and others crowd the frame, so the full outline takes some study.

Two large pale-green leaves held by a hand in front of mottled peeling trunk bark, over a ground of dry grass and brown litter. The leaves are the main subject, but they overlap, the hand touches the edge of one, and the busy background competes; the litter suggests autumn.

One large green leaf, whole and sharply lit, against plain lawn, with its broad lobes, toothed edge and pale veins easy to read. Its stalk runs off the bottom of the frame, so the stalk-to-twig join is not shown.

A leafy shoot with several overlapping green leaves, the top-left one showing its lobed outline in full, against a blurred autumn-coloured background. The leaves crowd one another and the edge teeth are small, so the margin needs a search.

A large backlit leaf seen from below, glowing yellow-green with strong veins, partly covered by a darker leaf above and set against a street scene with deep shadows. The view from below and the backlight change its look, and the overlap and clutter make the outline and edge harder to trace.

One large green leaf on a dark plain background, upper side, with a sharp outline and coarse teeth. Other leaves overlap at the top and the twig joins show only partly, so arrangement is a search; the brown blotches are on neighbouring leaves and do not change the main outline.

Forked, hollow trunk seen from a distance with the cream-and-brown mottled bark readable on the left stem. The surface texture needs a search at this range, and the busy green undergrowth competes with the trunk.

One whole pale-green leaf on gravel with a clear lobed outline, toothed edge and palmate veins. The petiole runs out of the frame so the twig join is not shown, and the pale stippling does not change the outline.
Leafless winter crown seen from below against blue sky. The main subject is the branch structure, not a leaf, bark area or fruit.
A cut leafy branch laid on grey decking, upper sides, with the petioles joining the stem. Several leaves overlap, but the top leaf shows its full outline and toothed edge against the plain boards.

Street-tree trunk in shade with a car, kerb and other trunks in the frame. The pale peeling patches at the base are visible, but the upper trunk is dark, so the pattern and colour need a search because of the shade.
Close view of a trunk with cream, olive and brown flaking patches. The trunk edges and a branch crossing in front are in the frame, and the background is soft.

Full-size bright green leaf with a clear toothed edge, but its right side merges with the leaves behind it, so the outline needs a search and the leaves are crowded. A small bud and tiny new leaves by the red twig are signs of new growth, so spring.

Pale mottled upper trunk and a branch seen from below against blue sky, with bare twigs in front. The mottled pattern is readable, but the upward angle and the thin twigs make the surface texture harder to study.
Frame filled by bark texture only, with olive, cream and orange-brown patches and no trunk edge, branch or scale object. The pattern repeat is clear.

A green seed ball of full round shape hangs from a stalk in front of a plain green leaf. It is unripe, so growth_stage is unripe and usual_look is false. The stalk shows but the twig does not, so hang is a search.

The flared base of a trunk beside a curb, with dark bark and pale flaking patches, seen from a distance. Texture and pattern are small in the frame, so both are search. The curb, grass, leaf litter and part of a red car compete, so alone is false.
A leafless crown with white upper trunk and branches against a blue sky, taken from below. The main subject is the crown, not a bark area, so part is other. The view from below is an angle cause.

A brown seed ball that has shed its seeds lies on a log, and the surface shows bare pits with no spiky hairs, so it is atypical. A second small ball, loose fluff and litter crowd the frame, so alone is false. It lies on a log, so hang is no. The round shape is clear, and kind needs close study.

A trunk fills the frame, with the typical mottled bark that peels in thin plates from brown to cream. The trunk edges show against a soft woodland background in good light. Texture, pattern and colour all read well.

Many small brown seed balls hang on bare twigs against a plain blue sky, shot from below. Each ball is only a few pixels wide, so kind and shape are search. Hang is clear because the balls show on the twigs. The view from below is an angle cause.

A pale trunk and its lowest branches seen from below, with leafy crown and neighbouring trees behind. The main subject is the tree form, so part is other. The view from below is an angle cause. A reader who took it as bark would give bark_up_or_dark.

A ripe round seed ball hangs on its stalk from a twig, in sharp focus against a soft blurred background. The ball looks golden, which suggests warm low sun, so light is a cause, but it does not hide the features.

A close-up of mottled bark in grey-green, cream, yellow and brown patches, with a lichen patch at the right and a knot in the middle. The frame shows texture only: no trunk edge, no branch and no scale object, so too_close is true. The pattern repeat is wide enough to read.

A fairly smooth pale grey-green trunk with small tan flakes and a knot, which looks like a young or small tree. The patches are low in contrast, so pattern is a search. Leaves in front of the trunk, side branches and a yellow plant at the base crowd the frame, so alone is false.

One dried seed ball hangs from a stalk against a soft sky, sharp and whole, but its face has opened into a fluffy tuft where the seeds have dispersed. The broken-open form is atypical, so it is after_seed_fall and not the usual look.

Several intact, ripe brown seed balls hang on long stalks from bare twigs against plain blue sky. The balls are small in the frame (about 25 px), so the fruit kind needs a close look (search), while the round outline and the hanging habit read clearly.

A large, green, palmately lobed leaf held in a hand, probably showing the paler underside with raised veins. A small, still-developing seed ball hangs on a fresh green stalk from a twig, with an unfurling leaf above and a soft green background. The new growth marks spring and the small early ball has not reached its full form, so it is young and not the usual look.
A full-size but still green seed ball hangs on a stalk from a twig, in focus against soft autumn-coloured leaves. It is unripe, so the usual look is false; the shape, kind and hang all read clearly.

A disintegrated seed ball lies on a log, seen from above as a flat brush of fluff around the brown core, with the stalk to the right. The broken form is atypical and the top view is an unusual angle, so the kind and the outline need close study, and the hang is not shown.

A full-size yellow-green seed ball hangs on a long green stalk from a twig, sharp against sky and bare trees. It has not yet turned brown, so it is unripe and not the usual look; the kind, outline and hang are clear.

A single seed ball hangs on a long thin stalk below bare twigs with buds, sharp against a soft grey background. The ball is small in the frame but the kind, the round outline and the hang are all readable.
A row of leafy trees along a path, so the main subject is a scene and the part is other. The source name matches the tree.

An avenue of London planetrees seen from below along a path, with crowns meeting overhead, so the main subject is a scene and the part is other. The source name Platanus x hispanica matches the tree, and the fruit depth feature does not apply.

Dense crown foliage where the leaves blend into a mass, with no single leaf as the subject. Only a few lobed outlines can be traced, no leaf edge is readable, and the bright sky behind the leaves washes out their colour (light).

Sharp, well-lit trunk with a wide area of mottled brown, cream and olive flaking bark and both trunk edges visible against a soft background. Nothing makes it harder.

One large lobed leaf, grey-green with raised pale veins (the underside), held in a hand against a dark soft background. The fingers cover part of the lower lobe and another leaf crosses the right side, so whole is false.

A branch seen from below against bright sky: the leaves are crowded and backlit, and their undersides show (angle, light). One small seed ball hangs at the lower right, but the leaves are the main subject, so I set part to leaf; the outline and teeth take close study.
A street scene with a row of leafy trees along a road and cyclists, so the main subject is none of leaf, bark or fruit.

One whole green leaf with clear lobes, coarse teeth and veins, in sharp focus against a dark soft background. The stalks of the neighbouring leaves meet at the lower left, but the twig itself is not shown.

A leafy branch seen from below against blue sky, with about eight small green seed balls hanging on long stalks; the leaves compete and the balls are small in the frame, so kind and shape are search. A pale trunk with a fine network of dark cracks between thin cream plates, trunk edges in view, and soft palm leaves and pots behind it. The fine crack pattern reads well.

Several large lobed green leaves overlap on a sunlit branch, with flaking trunk bark and power lines also in the frame. The leaves crowd each other so alone is false and the margin is search; the strong sun washes some leaves to yellow-green.
A full trunk width with the classic mottled grey-green and cream patch pattern, trunk edges visible, and a soft green forest behind it. Sharp and well lit.
A tight crop of rough, thick, flaking bark with no trunk edge, branch, or scale. The right half is in deep shadow, which changes the colour and makes the plate pattern search.
A close crop of smooth camouflage patches in green, yellow, cream, and brown, with no trunk edge, branch, or scale, so too_close is true. The colours are vivid but look natural and not filtered.
A narrow, sharp trunk with brown and cream peeling patches in front of a plain white wall and window. Both trunk edges show, and the small file size is not a fault.

Dense foliage of many overlapping green leaves, with a few pale undersides and tiny fruit balls far off. One central leaf can be traced with effort, but the others blend into a mass, so shape and margin are at search and the leaf is not alone or whole.

A scene in low warm sun: blurred brown autumn leaves in front, a trunk, and one small green seed ball far off on a thin stalk. No part is the main subject; the warm low sun and shadows change the colour (light).
One sharp yellow-green spiny seed ball hangs from a stalk in front of dark green leaves. Kind, shape and hang are easy to read; the ball is green and not yet ripe, and only one ball shows.
A small file of one green-yellow spiny seed ball hanging on a long thin stalk against a soft green background. The ball is sharp enough to read and is not ripe; only one ball shows.

Several dark brown seed balls hang on separate stalks, seen from below against a blue sky. The balls are dark from backlight (light) and the view is from below (angle); the shapes and the bristly surface can still be read, and no two balls share one stalk.

One small dark brown seed ball hangs on a stalk in the middle of large green leaves, seen from below with the sun behind. The ball is small and in shade (light, angle), so kind and shape are at search, and the leaves compete in the frame.

Pale green spiny seed balls hang in a chain on one stalk under a large leaf, with a third ball partly hidden behind it. The two balls on one stalk and the thin stalk between them show clearly; the fruit is green and not yet ripe.

One dry brown spiky seed ball held in a hand against soft fallen-leaf litter; the round outline and the bristly ball texture read clearly. The ball hangs from nothing visible and only a short stalk end shows at the hand, so hang is no, and there is a single ball, so two_heads is no.

One red-and-green autumn maple leaf with three clear lobes on a dark-tipped stalk, set against conifer twigs and other leaves. The margin is serrate but only a close look shows the teeth, so it is search. Autumn colour is not a cause.

A ground litter of many fallen red, pink and brown leaves that blend into one mass, and the leaves are dead fallen leaves. No single leaf outline can be read as the subject.

A young shrub or sapling with a trunk and many red and green maple leaves overlapping, so the leaves blend into a mass across the frame. Individual lobes need search, and the colour is autumn colour, not a cause.

One whole red maple leaf with three clear lobes lies on the forest floor, but brown fallen leaves compete in the background. The leaf is red, not brown, so it is not a dead leaf. Margin and veins need close study.
A branch of full-size green mature maple leaves, with many leaves overlapping. Each lobe is visible only with study, so shape and margin are search, and no leaf is whole.

A wide landscape scene with a shrub of red and orange leaves, blue asters and water behind. The main subject is a scene and a shrub, not one leaf, so the part is other and the leaves blend into a mass.
A close cluster of yellow, orange and red maple leaves on one branch, with the central leaf partly covered by others. Lobes and margin need close study, and the colour is autumn colour.

One whole green mature maple leaf with three clear lobes, a toothed margin and clear veins, on a red stalk against a soft dark background. The stalk does not show where it joins the twig, so arrangement is no.

A large red-and-green autumn maple leaf in the foreground with clear lobes, with other leaves crowding the frame behind it. The margin and veins need close study, and the autumn colour is not a cause.

A crown of yellow autumn foliage with a red-leaved tree and a building behind, so the main subject is a crown and the part is other. The leaves fill the frame as a mass and the scene is busy, so alone is false; autumn colour is not a cause.
A whole mossy trunk seen from a distance in a woodland. Moss hides the ridges, so texture and pattern need close study, and the colour is green moss over grey-brown bark.

Three trunks of a multi-stem tree at a medium distance, with a cavity in the middle stem that is a hole in the trunk. The middle stem sits in shadow, which changes its colour, and the ridges read only with close study.
A close fill-frame view of grey-brown plates, ridges and fissures with some lichen. The frame shows texture only, with no trunk edge, branch or scale object.
A full-width view of a tall grey trunk with long vertical ridges and shaggy plates, with the trunk edges and woodland behind. The features read clearly at this size.
A close view of reddish-brown and grey bark with scaly plates and horizontal fissures, with a thin twig at the top left. The texture and pattern read clearly.
The camera looks up the trunk into the crown, with strong backlight and flare washing the colour. The birdhouse competes for attention, and the ridges read only with close study.
A close fill-frame view of grey-brown bark with long vertical ridges and plates. The frame shows texture only, with no trunk edge, branch or scale object, and the features read clearly.

A slender trunk is a small part of a woodland scene with autumn leaves on the ground, so the main subject is the scene and the part is other. The trunk runs off the top of the frame and the background trees compete with it.
A fill-frame view of grey-brown bark with long shaggy ridges and plates, with a hand touching the left edge. The hand is a scale object and covers little of the bark.

Red samaras hang in clusters across a crowded branch in front of pine needles, and several clusters are cut by the frame edge, so whole and alone are false. The samaras are still red, so they are unripe.
Pink-tan samaras hang from red stalks against soft green leaves, sharp and fully shown with wings clear. The pink colour marks them as unripe.
A whole trunk seen from a few metres in grass, with the trunk edge visible. The ridges and plates are readable only with close study, so texture and pattern are search.
A close view of pink-green samaras in a cluster on a soft green background, with wings and stalks clear. The pink colour marks them as unripe.
Deep vertical ridges and pale patches fill the frame with no trunk edge, branch, or scale object, so the photo is texture only and too_close is true. The ridge pattern reads clearly.
Reddish-tan samaras hang from a thin branch against a plain blue sky, with wings readable. The colour marks them as unripe.
Pale green samaras hang among fresh leaves on a crowded branch, so alone is false. Wing outlines are small, so shape and wing are search, and the samaras are unripe.
Pale flaking plates fill the frame with no trunk edge, branch, or scale object, so too_close is true. The plates and grey-brown colour read clearly.
Pink-green samaras hang from red stems among soft-focus green leaves, with wings clear. The pink colour marks them as unripe.

Red maple samaras hang in clusters from a twig against a soft, blurred background. The paired samaras and their wings are clear. The fruit is still bright pink-red and not yet brown, so it is unripe and not the usual look.

Several green sugar maple leaves on a branch in a park. The lower-left leaf is cut off by the frame edge and partly hidden by the twig, so whole is false and the crowded leaves make alone false. Red maple samara clusters hang from bare twigs against a black background, lit like a flash photo. The samara shape, wings and the way the clusters hang are clear. The fruit is still red, not brown, so it is unripe. The flash light changes the colour, so light is a cause.

A whole green sugar maple leaf on a black background, lit evenly, with a clear outline and visible veins. The margin is coarse and needs a closer look (search). Nothing else in the frame competes with the leaf.

Red maple flower clusters hang from a bare twig against a pale sky, with no leaves or fruit shown. The photo's main subject is flowers, which take the place of the feature, so it is rejected as buds_or_flowers.

A pile of fallen sugar maple leaves in red, orange and yellow autumn colours. The central leaf is overlapped by others, so whole is false and alone is false. The lobes and margin need close study (search). Autumn colour is not a cause, and the leaves are not brown or dead.

Red maple samaras hang in clusters from a twig against a plain blue sky. The paired wings and the clusters are clear. The samaras are reddish-brown and mature, so they are ripe and show the usual look.

A whole sugar maple leaf lying on wood mulch. The lobes and veins are clear, and the margin needs close study (search). The cool, shaded light makes the leaf look blue-green, so light is a cause. The photo is not tinted or filtered in a way that changes the tree.

A crown of orange autumn foliage seen from a distance. The leaves are small and blend into a mass, so the margin cannot be read (no) and the photo is rejected as leaf_mass and feature_unclear. Autumn colour is not a cause.

A twig with several hanging samara clusters among green Acer leaves on a black background. The samara kind and how the clusters hang are clear. The outline and wing are small in the frame, so a learner must look closely at them.
